Hi all — quick technical notes and proposed preflight items. Attaching a terse ports checklist (network_ports_and_firewall_rules.txt).

Summary recommendations:
- For initial rollout we recommend VPC peering when: ultra-low latency between your apps and the inference endpoint is required and you control both VPCs. PrivateLink (NLB + interface endpoints) is preferable when you want explicit per-service access and avoid route table complexity. Both are supported by Redwood.
- Transit Gateway is supported but overlapping CIDRs complicate route selection; if Aureline must retain overlapping CIDRs we should use PrivateLink or set up a Transit Gateway with NAT/transit rules — this adds network engineering work and slightly higher latency.
- On-prem package option: if they require an edge appliance with BGP, we need their BGP ASN, public IPs for BGP peering, and firewall permissions on ports 179 (BGP), 443, and 10250-10255 (if they plan to host host-agent comms).

Preflight checklist (high level):
1) Share VPC CIDRs and network diagram
2) Confirm whether they prefer VPC Peering or PrivateLink
3) Open ports: 443 (TCP), 10250-10255 (TCP) for agent control plane, 50051 (gRPC) if using grpc ingestion, 5222/5223 only for optional health probes
4) Provide a bastion/bounce host IP for runbook access or add our jump-host to allow temporary SSH (if appliance install required)
5) If on-prem BGP: provide ASN + candidate public IPs

I'll draft a compact preflight doc (attached) we can send to Aureline. I can also run a lightweight connectivity test during the proposed window to confirm routing.

Attachment: network_ports_and_firewall_rules.txt
